body.name: Deterministic-prefix plug-in design
body.construction: Construct \(d^{\mathrm{pre}}_{n,B}\) as follows. Among all positive integer partitions with \(m_b\ge4\), \(\sum_bm_b=n\), and \(m_b\in4\mathbb N\) for \(b<B\), take the lexicographically first minimizer of \(F_{n,B}(m)\), and put \(w_b=m_b/n\). For each \(b\) and \(h\in\mathsf H_{b-1}\), let \(k_b=\lfloor T_{b-1}/4\rfloor\) and \(\mathcal K_b=\{\lceil m_b/4\rceil,\ldots,\lfloor3m_b/4\rfloor\}\). If \(k_b<2\), define \(q_b(h)\) as the element \(k\in\mathcal K_b\) minimizing \(|k-m_b/2|\), with the smaller \(k\) breaking a tie. If \(k_b\ge2\), define \(q_b(h)\) as the element \(k\in\mathcal K_b\) minimizing \(\widehat v_1(k_b;h)/(k/m_b)+\widehat v_0(k_b;h)/(1-k/m_b)\), again with the smaller \(k\) breaking a tie. These finite-valued tie-broken argmin rules are Borel maps on \((\mathsf H_{b-1},\mathcal G_{b-1})\). The law \(P^{d^{\mathrm{pre}}_{n,B}}_{\mu,\sigma}\) is the recursive canonical law in def:observed-adaptive-law generated by these maps.
